    Home/Learn/Best peptides for muscle growth: what the evidence shows

    Best peptides for muscle growth: what the evidence in people shows.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Checked 30 Oct 2026.

    Short answer

    No peptide is FDA approved for building muscle. Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is approved to reduce belly fat in adults with HIV and lipodystrophy, and growth hormone itself (somatropin) mainly for growth hormone deficiency.12 CJC-1295 and ipamorelin are research-use peptides. We found no trial in people that shows any of them builds muscle.

    Which peptides are sold for muscle?

    Our muscle page lists the options people ask about:

    • Sermorelin: No FDA-approved product on the market. A growth-hormone-releasing shot from compounding pharmacies; the approved brand was taken off the market years ago.
    • CJC-1295 / ipamorelin: Not approved. Growth-hormone-releasing peptides sold by research-use shops and some clinics. No approved product, no large human trials.
    • IGF-1 LR3: Not approved. A modified form of IGF-1, a hormone the body makes in response to growth hormone. No approved product; the approved IGF-1 medicine, mecasermin (Increlex), is a different product.
    • Tesamorelin (Egrifta): FDA approved. A daily shot approved only to reduce belly fat in people with HIV. Sold off-label by clinics for "growth hormone".
    • Testosterone (TRT): FDA approved. Replaces a hormone the body makes too little of. Not FDA approved for low testosterone without an associated medical condition.

    Most of them work on the same signal. They make the body release more growth hormone, which is why they are called growth hormone secretagogues. CJC-1295 is a long-acting copy of the hormone that tells the body to release growth hormone.3 Ipamorelin acts on a different receptor with the same aim.4

    What has been tested in people?

    Hormone levels, not muscle. In two placebo-controlled trials in healthy adults, CJC-1295 raised growth hormone and IGF-I, a hormone made in response to it, for days after each injection.3 The trials measured those hormones and side effects; they did not measure muscle or strength.

    Ipamorelin was developed in rats and pigs.4 Its one larger trial in people was for a different problem: 117 patients after bowel surgery, where it did no better than a placebo.5

    We found no trial in people that shows CJC-1295, ipamorelin or sermorelin builds muscle. A higher hormone level in a blood test is not the same as more muscle.

    Why are they on the FDA's risk list for compounding?

    The FDA keeps a list of substances that may be risky when pharmacies use them to make medicines.6 The FDA says ipamorelin may set off an immune reaction when given some ways, and that a published study found serious side effects, including a death, when it was given into a vein for gut problems.6

    The FDA lists serious side effects linked to CJC-1295, including a faster heart rate and a reaction in which blood vessels widen across the body, and says the data in people are limited.6

    What is approved, and for what?

    Tesamorelin is approved to reduce excess belly fat in adults with HIV who have lipodystrophy, a change in where the body stores fat. Its label says it is not for weight loss.1 It is not approved for muscle.

    Somatropin is growth hormone made in a lab. It is approved for children who do not grow because of growth hormone deficiency or some other conditions, and for adults with growth hormone deficiency.2 It is not approved for building muscle in healthy people.

    A doctor decides whether you have a condition they treat.

    What do they cost?

    We show shop prices once the shops are in our database.

    A price per mg says nothing about what is in a vial. Our guide on how to read a COA shows what a lab report can tell you, and How we rate explains the five checks next to each shop.

    So what are the best peptides for muscle?

    On the evidence in people, none. The peptides sold for muscle raise hormone levels in short trials or were tested for other problems, and the FDA lists safety concerns for two of them. The approved growth hormone medicines are for medical conditions.

    None of this is medical advice. A doctor can tell you what fits your goal.

    Questions about peptides for muscle growth

    What are the best peptides for muscle growth?

    On the evidence in people, none. The peptides sold for muscle raise hormone levels in short trials or were tested for other problems, and the FDA lists safety concerns for two of them.

    Is any peptide FDA approved for building muscle?

    No. Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is approved to reduce belly fat in adults with HIV and lipodystrophy, and growth hormone itself (somatropin) mainly for growth hormone deficiency.

    Do CJC-1295 and ipamorelin build muscle?

    We found no trial in people that shows CJC-1295, ipamorelin or sermorelin builds muscle. In two trials in healthy adults, CJC-1295 raised growth hormone and IGF-I; the trials did not measure muscle or strength.

    What has the FDA said about CJC-1295 and ipamorelin?

    The FDA lists serious side effects linked to CJC-1295, including a faster heart rate, and says the data in people are limited. For ipamorelin, it says a published study found serious side effects, including a death, when it was given into a vein for gut problems.
